source.title: ROCKET: Residual-Oriented Multi-Layer Alignment for Spatially-Aware Vision-Language-Action Models
source.authors: Guoheng Sun; Tingting Du; Kaixi Feng; Chenxiang Luo; Xingguo Ding; Zheyu Shen; Ziyao Wang; Yexiao He; Ang Li

record.tranche_reason: The study measures cross-model representation similarity and reports that it varies by layer depth, refining the scope of claims about alignment. It does not test whether alignment rises with model scale or capability.
record.gate_note: The relevant result is the layer-wise CKA comparison of OpenVLA-7B and VGGT. LIBERO success rates, gradient cosine similarities, and projector-weight similarities are not results measuring representational convergence and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a VLA training-method paper. It uses representation alignment to a frozen VGGT teacher as a tool and reports task success rates for its own method. Its one cross-model similarity result is a single layer-wise linear CKA diagnostic of OpenVLA-7B against VGGT (Appendix F, Fig. 8). That diagnostic only motivates the sparse-activation design. It has one model pair, one metric, no scale or capability sweep, no comparison across metrics or inputs, and no numbers in the text. The text also does not say whether the OpenVLA representations were measured before or after alignment training; if after, the similarity was induced by the method. Layer-depth dependence is not one of the dependencies V6 names (the similarity measure, its settings, the inputs), so the result bears on no version as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: The record paraphrases only the appendix CKA observation. The authors' main conclusion is about their method. ROCKET is multi-layer alignment with a shared projector plus Matryoshka-style sparse activation. It reduces the gradient interference of naive multi-projector alignment and reaches 98.5% on LIBERO with about 4% of prior compute. It also generalizes across LIBERO-Plus, RoboTwin and several VLA backbones. The CKA result (shallow VGGT layers are more similar and easier to align) is a side observation used to motivate the sparse activation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses linear CKA for a layer-wise comparison of one VLA and one 3D vision model; it does not perform a model-scale or capability sweep, or compare alternative similarity measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported CKA similarity varies by layer depth.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear CKA between OpenVLA-7B vision tokens and VGGT features is higher for shallow VGGT layers and generally declines with depth (Fig. 8; values not in text).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-model representational similarity between a 2D VLA and a 3D vision model depends on the layer depth compared.

record.problems: The CKA result is for one model pair and one similarity measure. Numerical CKA values and uncertainty estimates are not stated in the text, and the figure is the only source for detailed values.
record.rows_left_out: No other results bearing on the claim's representation-similarity versions were reported. Task success, gradient cosine, and projector-weight cosine results were left out because they do not measure representational convergence.

untested.parts: Whole version: no scale or capability sweep, no set of independently trained models.
Whole version: no image-caption paired alignment between vision and language models.
Whole version: no comparison across seeds of one architecture.
Whole version. A learned projector is used for distillation, but mapping loss between models is never reported.
Whole version: no feature or circuit analysis.
Whole version: no comparison of metrics, metric settings or input sets, and no in- versus out-of-distribution test.
Whole version: no assessment of plateau, incompleteness or causes of alignment.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's relation 'tests'/T5 is overturned: this is a T4 tool use with an incidental diagnostic. Other similarity measures in the paper are excluded as non-representational or within-model: gradient cosine, projector-weight cosine, and within-model input/output cosine used for layer selection (Fig. 15).

versions.untested_parts: Whether alignment rises as models get larger or more capable, and whether independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, and data converge.
Alignment between vision and language models on paired images and captions, and whether it rises as both models improve.
Representations across random seeds of the same architecture and shared features or subspaces.
Whether one model's representations can be mapped to another's with little loss, including linear mapping, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired mapping.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across models.
The study reports variation by layer depth, but does not compare similarity metrics, metric settings beyond layer choice, input datasets, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs.
Whether alignment is incomplete or plateaus, or whether shared training data or objectives explain it.

rows.subject: OpenVLA-7B and VGGT
rows.operation_detail: Compute linear CKA between OpenVLA vision-token representations and VGGT visual features across layers.

conditions.value: layer-wise comparison; shallow and deeper VGGT layers
held-out samples; sample count not stated
VGGT features resampled to OpenVLA vision-token layout

rows.value: Shallow VGGT layers are more similar to OpenVLA-7B; similarity generally decreases with depth.
rows.note: The text describes the layer-wise trend; it does not give numerical CKA values.
rows.check: Layer-wise CKA between one student VLA and one 3D teacher varies with depth. That is not variation by similarity measure, metric settings or inputs, so it does not bear on V6, and no version predicts a layer profile. The training stage of the student when measured is unspecified, so the similarity may be induced by alignment training. No numerical values are given in the text.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
